posts.title: A plum blossom walk
posts.excerpt: The old plum by the temple gate opens first. Here is a slow loop that passes it twice.
posts.content:
Leave the shop, turn left along the canal and cross the second bridge. The temple lane climbs gently, and the plum stands just inside the gate.

Come back by the tea houses for a cup of hot amazake, then pass the plum again on the way down; the light is softer by then.

posts.title: Kimono in the rain
posts.excerpt: Rain is no reason to cancel. A few small tricks keep the hem dry and the day lovely.
posts.content:
On wet days we lift the hem a finger higher, give you rain covers for the sandals and lend a crimson paper umbrella at no charge.

Wet stone lanes shine like lacquer, and the lanterns glow brighter. Some of our favourite photos were taken in the rain.

posts.title: An afternoon at the tea house
posts.excerpt: Three tea houses within five minutes of the shop, and what to order at each.
posts.content:
The red-felt benches on the canal are for matcha and a skewer of grilled dango. Sit on the edge; the obi bow likes the space.

Further up, the quiet house behind the bamboo serves cold sweet bean soup in summer and hot in winter. Ask for the window seat.
